stem: The foundational ancient treatise on Indian dramaturgy and dance is the __________.
solution: The Natya Shastra is the foundational treatise on drama, dance and music.

stem: The Natya Shastra is attributed to the sage __________.
solution: The Natya Shastra is attributed to Bharata Muni.

stem: The text 'Abhinaya Darpana', an important manual on gesture in dance, was written by __________.
solution: The Abhinaya Darpana ('Mirror of Gesture') was written by Nandikeshwara.

stem: The national academy that officially recognises India's classical dance forms is the __________.
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises the classical dance and music forms.

stem: The three aspects of Indian classical dance are Nritta, Natya and __________.
solution: Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressional dance) and Natya (dramatic element) are the three aspects.

stem: 'Nritta' in Indian classical dance refers to __________.
solution: Nritta is pure dance — rhythmic movement without expressing a theme.

stem: The vigorous, masculine aspect of dance is called Tandava, while the graceful, feminine aspect is called __________.
solution: Tandava is the vigorous masculine aspect; Lasya is the graceful feminine aspect.

stem: The term 'Abhinaya' in Indian dance refers to __________.
solution: Abhinaya is the art of expression (facial, gestural) used to convey emotion and meaning.

stem: The classical dance form of Tamil Nadu is __________.
solution: Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu.

stem: Bharatanatyam evolved from the temple dance tradition of the __________.
solution: Bharatanatyam evolved from the Devadasi (temple dancer) tradition of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The person credited with reviving Bharatanatyam in the 20th century and founding Kalakshetra was __________.
options: Rukmini Devi only as a critic
solution: Rukmini Devi Arundale revived Bharatanatyam and founded the Kalakshetra institution.

stem: The basic units of footwork in Bharatanatyam are called __________.
solution: Adavus are the basic units of footwork/steps in Bharatanatyam.

stem: The classical dance form associated with North India and the Kathakars (storytellers) is __________.
solution: Kathak, from North India, developed from the Kathakars (storytellers).

stem: The only classical dance form performed to Hindustani (North Indian) music is __________.
solution: Kathak is the only classical dance set to Hindustani classical music.

stem: Kathak developed distinctive court styles under the __________ influence.
solution: Kathak flourished and refined its court style under Mughal patronage.

stem: The three main gharanas (schools) of Kathak are Lucknow, Jaipur and __________.
solution: The main Kathak gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras (with Raigarh as a later one).

stem: The legendary Kathak exponent of the Lucknow gharana, Birju Maharaj, belonged to which art?
solution: Pandit Birju Maharaj was a legendary Kathak exponent of the Lucknow gharana.

stem: The rapid pirouettes (spins) characteristic of Kathak are called __________.
solution: Chakkars are the fast spins characteristic of Kathak.

stem: The elaborate dance-drama of Kerala with heavy make-up and costumes is __________.
solution: Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala with elaborate make-up and costume.

stem: In Kathakali, the green (pacha) facial make-up denotes a __________ character.
solution: Green (pacha) make-up in Kathakali denotes noble, virtuous heroic characters.

stem: Kathakali performances traditionally draw their themes from the __________.
solution: Kathakali dramatises stories from the Hindu epics, the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

stem: The classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh is __________.
solution: Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh.

stem: Kuchipudi is traditionally associated with the saint-composer __________.
solution: Kuchipudi is associated with the saint Siddhendra Yogi.

stem: A special item of Kuchipudi in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate is the __________.
solution: The tarangam is a Kuchipudi item danced on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot.

stem: The classical dance form of Odisha is __________.
solution: Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha.

stem: The characteristic body posture of Odissi, with a three-fold bend of the body, is the __________.
solution: The tribhanga (three-bend) is the signature posture of Odissi.

stem: Odissi is closely linked with the temple of __________.
solution: Odissi is closely linked with the Jagannath temple at Puri.

stem: The temple dancers of Odisha were called Maharis, while the young boys who danced dressed as girls were the __________.
solution: The Maharis were female temple dancers; the Gotipuas were boy dancers of Odissi.

stem: The Odissi maestro who greatly revived and popularised the form was __________.
solution: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Odissi exponent and revivalist.

stem: The classical dance form of Manipur is __________.
solution: Manipuri is the classical dance of Manipur.

stem: The Manipuri dance is centred on the theme of __________.
options: Ras Lila of Radha and Krishna
solution: Manipuri dance centres on the Ras Lila, the divine love of Radha and Krishna.

stem: A distinctive feature of Manipuri dance compared with other classical forms is its __________.
options: gentle, graceful movements with restrained facial expression
solution: Manipuri is marked by gentle, gliding movements and subdued facial expression, without heavy ankle bells.

stem: The drum used in Manipuri dance (Cholom) is the __________.
solution: The Pung (a barrel drum) is central to Manipuri dance, especially the Pung Cholom.

stem: The graceful solo female dance of Kerala, meaning 'dance of the enchantress', is __________.
solution: Mohiniyattam ('dance of Mohini, the enchantress') is the graceful female dance of Kerala.

stem: Mohiniyattam is dominated by the __________ aspect of dance.
solution: Mohiniyattam is dominated by the Lasya (graceful, feminine) aspect.

stem: The costume of a Mohiniyattam dancer is typically __________.
solution: Mohiniyattam dancers wear a distinctive white costume with a gold border.

stem: The classical dance form of Assam, associated with Vaishnava monasteries, is __________.
solution: Sattriya is the classical dance of Assam.

stem: Sattriya dance was introduced by the 15th–16th century Vaishnava saint __________.
solution: Sattriya was introduced by the Assamese saint Srimanta Sankardeva.

stem: Sattriya dance is performed in the Vaishnava monasteries of Assam called __________.
solution: Sattriya is performed in the Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) of Assam.

stem: Sattriya was granted classical dance status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year __________.
solution: Sattriya was recognised as a classical dance form in the year 2000.

stem: The semi-classical masked dance form of eastern India with Purulia, Seraikella and Mayurbhanj styles is __________.
solution: Chhau is a semi-classical masked/martial dance with Purulia, Seraikella and Mayurbhanj styles.

stem: Chhau dance has been inscribed on the UNESCO list of __________.
solution: Chhau dance is on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

stem: The number of classical dance forms currently recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi is __________.
solution: Eight classical dance forms are recognised (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya).

stem: The hand gestures used in Indian classical dance are called __________.
solution: Mudras (hastas) are the codified hand gestures of Indian classical dance.

stem: The concept of 'Rasa' in Indian aesthetics refers to __________.
options: the emotional flavour/sentiment evoked in the audience
solution: Rasa is the aesthetic sentiment or emotional flavour evoked in the spectator.

stem: The traditional solo repertoire (margam) of Bharatanatyam usually opens with the __________.
solution: The Bharatanatyam margam traditionally opens with the Alarippu, a pure-dance invocation.

stem: The dance-drama tradition 'Yakshagana' belongs to the state of __________.
solution: Yakshagana is a traditional dance-drama of Karnataka.

stem: The rhythmic syllables recited in Indian classical dance are called __________.
solution: Rhythmic syllables (bols in Kathak, sollukattu in Bharatanatyam) accompany the footwork.

stem: The pioneering modern dancer who blended Indian dance with Western techniques in the early 20th century was __________.
solution: Uday Shankar pioneered a modern, creative fusion of Indian and Western dance.

stem: The classical dance in which the dancer traditionally holds a lit lamp or dances with a pot is most associated with __________.
solution: Kuchipudi is famous for items involving balancing a pot and dancing on a brass plate.

stem: Bharatanatyam was earlier known by the name __________.
solution: Bharatanatyam was earlier known as Sadir or Dasi Attam in the Devadasi tradition.

stem: The 'ashtanayika' concept, depicting eight types of heroines, is a common theme in __________ dance.
solution: The ashtanayika (eight heroines) is a recurring expressive theme in Indian classical dance.

stem: The Bharatanatyam item that is the centrepiece combining pure and expressive dance is the __________.
solution: The Varnam is the elaborate centrepiece of a Bharatanatyam recital, combining nritta and abhinaya.

stem: The Manipuri Ras Lila is traditionally performed during the festival of __________.
solution: The Manipuri Ras Lila is performed during Krishna-related festivals such as those in Kartik.

stem: The classical dances are broadly rooted in the tradition of the __________.
solution: The classical dances trace their theoretical roots to the Natya Shastra.

stem: The dance form 'Kathakali' literally means __________.
solution: Kathakali means 'story-play' (katha = story, kali = play/performance).

stem: In Kathakali, the elaborate make-up and painted face is called __________.
solution: The elaborate Kathakali make-up (with the chutti and coloured vesham) transforms the actor.

stem: The percussion instrument central to Kathakali and many Kerala arts is the __________.
solution: The Chenda is the main percussion instrument in Kathakali and Kerala temple arts.

stem: The dance form of Kerala that is purely a female solo, distinct from Kathakali, is __________.
solution: Mohiniyattam is the graceful female solo dance of Kerala, distinct from the dramatic Kathakali.

stem: Kalakshetra, the famous institution for Bharatanatyam, is located in __________.
solution: Kalakshetra, founded by Rukmini Devi Arundale, is in Chennai.

stem: The classical dance forms are performed with three basic elements: bhava, raga and __________.
solution: The words Bha (bhava/expression), Ra (raga/melody) and Ta (tala/rhythm) are traditionally seen as forming 'Bharata'.

stem: Which classical dance form originated as a solo temple dance and is known for its geometric lines and 'araimandi' half-sitting posture?
solution: Bharatanatyam is known for its geometric lines and the araimandi (half-sitting) posture.

stem: The two basic postures of Odissi are the tribhanga and the __________.
solution: The two basic Odissi postures are tribhanga and chowk (a square, Jagannath-like stance).

stem: The classical dances of India are significant because they combine __________.
solution: Indian classical dances integrate dance, music, drama and devotional expression.

stem: The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in the year __________.
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952–53 as India's national academy for performing arts.
